cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 answers T4's belonging reading with a rival; T6 maps both to actions.
cells.limitation: T3 sets aside T1 and T2 wholesale rather than engaging either argument.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T9 introduces irreversibility, absent from openings; T10 builds the dividing line from it.
cells.limitation: T11's persistence test arrives late and is not tested by another mind.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Crowd as noise (T1, T4) versus crowd as evidence (T2, T8) examined across turns.
cells.limitation: What the user values instead of milestones is never examined by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 concedes real clocks; T9 limits own method; T11 keeps disagreement open.
cells.limitation: T10's dividing line is accepted without Gilbert or Ibarra testing it.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T10 sharpens the open question: obey or outlast the discomfort.
cells.limitation: Section D's wisdom-versus-avoidance tension was never argued in the debate.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 states the strongest case for others' experience as evidence against T1.
cells.limitation: T3 labels Gilbert's lived-experience argument armchair reasoning, misreading T2.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T9 names reversibility as the assumption and where it breaks; T10 answers.
cells.limitation: T11's persists-means-data test goes unchallenged though exposure could sustain it.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T9 accurately notes Ibarra studied career changers, not marriage decisions.
cells.limitation: Runner flags one pd=false quotation; only visible candidate is T6 possessive friends'.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 and T5 label readings as possible and rival, not findings.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the feeling is mostly news about the crowd without qualification.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 names a flaw in its own source; T7 concedes biology and money.
cells.limitation: Skeptic never answers T8's point that friends' contentment is partial evidence.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A separates the feeling from wanting milestones and lists four candidate sources.
cells.limitation: Whether the user seeks permission not to want these goes unasked.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T6 ties belonging versus closing window to different actions for this user.
cells.limitation: T3's experiments draw on assumed context rather than the user's stated details.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T10 honours the user's uncertainty: wait until the wanting is truly yours.
cells.limitation: The user's own goals beyond milestones are never asked about.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E branches on finances, health or wanting children as real deadlines.
cells.limitation: T3 assumes the user is single; T11 assumes photo-scrolling. Neither was stated.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E turns each candidate source of the feeling into a branch with its implication.
cells.limitation: Relationship status is assumed in T3 instead of asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T4 belonging and T5 expiring options offered as rivals; D asks what it points at.
cells.limitation: The possibility the user wants these things but distrusts the want is absent.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 exposes the assumed schedule; T7 asks who set the expiry dates.
cells.limitation: Milestones as the measure of progress are questioned but no alternative measure explored.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T5-T6 surface closeness versus keeping doors open as conflicting goods.
cells.limitation: What the user values instead of milestones stays unasked across T1-T11.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T4 names fear of drifting from friends without pathologising it.
cells.limitation: Family or parental expectations, a common source of feeling behind, never raised.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D offers readings to recognize or reject and a self-check question.
cells.limitation: T7 tells the user to name a clock without offering how to tell.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E lists investing in friendships, acting on a clock, outlasting, experimenting.
cells.limitation: The choice itself is never stated plainly; options emerge only in Section E.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: Section E notes waiting has actual costs when a real deadline exists.
cells.limitation: T3's experiments, such as renting somewhere new, carry unstated costs.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T11 and E: feeling fades without comparison favours outlasting; persists favours acting.
cells.limitation: T8's ask three friends uses a number not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names the source of the feeling as the deciding unknown.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not explicitly set apart from the consequential one.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: reversible experiments and honest friend conversations, irreversible choices held.
cells.limitation: T3's rent somewhere new is larger than the small step it claims.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T10 states the dividing line in plain words: try reversible, wait on irreversible.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 that fits points to T4; T9 good experiment points to T8.
cells.limitation: T11's that disagreement refers to T10's unsettled question, not a stated disagreement.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Eleven turns, all within range per deterministic checks; each carries one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Skeptic's rhetorical questions, Psychologist's cautions, Experimenter's action lists stay distinct.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths and cadence are close across all three minds.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; T6 links two readings to actions in one move.
cells.limitation: Section E repeats Section D's three readings almost item for item.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T7 raises real clocks of biology and money against borrowed schedules.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete loss is dramatised for the user.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T10 Skeptic adopts irreversibility as the line, citing T9's admission.
cells.limitation: Reversals are modest concessions rather than surprising turns.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T1 Behind what, exactly? and T3 arguing from armchairs give sharp voices.
cells.limitation: Psychologist's turns T8 and T11 read as cautious qualifiers with little flavour.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T4: a sample taken while everyone cheers measures the cheering.
cells.limitation: No humour; T11's closing line lands plainly.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9's self-critique shifts the debate's direction toward a resolution.
cells.limitation: Near-uniform turn lengths keep tempo flat from T1 to T11.

strengths: T9 Experimenter names a limit of its own source, and T10 builds the irreversibility line from it.
T4 and T5 offer belonging and expiring options as rival readings, and Section E branches on each.
T2 and T8 Psychologist challenge crowd-as-noise with a fair, accurate case for others' experience as evidence.
weaknesses: No mind asks what the user values instead of milestones; T7 and T10 leave their own measure blank.
T3 Experimenter assumes the user is single and T11 assumes photo-scrolling; neither was stated.
T3 dismisses T2's lived-experience argument as armchair reasoning, misreading the Psychologist's point.

symptoms.observed: Debate contests borrowed milestones but never asks what the user values instead.
symptoms.evidence: make the person name their own clock rather than borrow

symptoms.observed: Assumes the user is single and scrolls friends' photos; neither appears in the situation.
Groups Gilbert's evidence-from-others argument with Thoreau's as armchair introspection.
symptoms.evidence: You are both arguing from armchairs.

symptoms.observed: Proposes renting somewhere new as a cheap trial without naming its cost.
symptoms.evidence: tour a few places with a friend, rent somewhere new

symptoms.observed: Proposes asking a specific number of friends not drawn from the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: Ask three of them for the unpolished version

findings.description: Runner counts one pd=false turn with quotation marks. Reading every pd=false turn, the only candidate is the plural possessive in T6 (friends' new schedules), which is an apostrophe, not a quotation mark. No quotation is present, so no cap applies.
T3 assumes the user is dating and single; T11 assumes the user scrolls friends' photos. The situation states neither.
Attributions to Gilbert (others' experience as better predictor) and Ibarra (career changers, small experiments) match my knowledge of those books; no source evidence attached.

rubric_fit_notes: The runner's pd=false quotation-mark check appears to be a false positive triggered by the plural possessive in T6; I found no quotation in any pd=false turn and applied no cap. The question is labelled decision but the user asks mainly about a feeling with no explicit choice; the decision cells were read as written, with Section E's branches serving as the options.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision question per the label, so the conditional branches in Section E were scored as the options and decisive conditions even though the user named no explicit choice.
